text.p: Companhia de Seguros Imperio is "comfortable" with its remaining 21 percent stake in Banco Portugues do Atlantico but could sell if its partner Banco Comercial Portugues wanted to boost its holding further, a senior official said.

"We feel comfortable with it (the stake). Obviously, if BCP decided it wanted to buy (it), we would consider it," said Vasco de Mello, chairman of Banco Mello and whose family group controls the insurer.
BCP, which already had 50 percent of BPA, boosted its share to 75 percent on Thursday, by buying part of the 46 percent previously held by Imperio.
The purchase was made at 2,800 escudos per share, the same price the two paid at the time of the buyout in 1995. BPA shares, which are highly illiquid, were trading at 2,461 escudos on Friday.
"When we bought the position, we had an agreement that protected us from eventual negative fluctuations," Vasco de Mello said.
He said that the purchase of the stake by BCP did not mean that the BCP/BPA group would now reduce its holding in Banco Mello which amounts, directly and indirectly, to some 17 percent.
